utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. May I first of all thank everyone for making yourselves available at such -- I was going to say unearthly -- at such an early hour. May I first of all take the appearance -- sorry, would the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-70-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I now take the appearances for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm Tom Hannis on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. I'm assisted by Christina Moeller on my immediate right, Caroline Edgerton at the far end, and our case manager Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hannis. For the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I am Theodore Scudder and I'm assisted here this morning by Dragan Ivetic. We represent the defendant Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scudder. Now, Mr. Lukic, could you stand, please. Are you able to hear the proceedings that are taking place here in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Just please be seated again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Scudder, the further appearance that is being conducted this morning is for the principal purpose of taking pleas from your client. It is for him to decide whether he requires the indictment to be read in full or whether he, on your advice, accepts that is unnecessary. Can you indicate the position to me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sreten Lukic acknowledges that he is the Sreten Lukic named in the indictment. He's received a copy of the indictment and had the advice of counsel in reviewing the indictment. He waives the formal reading of it, and he enters a plea of not guilty to each of the counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scudder. Now, Mr. Lukic, could you stand again, please. You've heard Mr. Scudder indicate to me that he is authorised to tender a plea on your behalf.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have heard that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, can you confirm to me that you have had a copy of the indictment and have read it and understood it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have received a copy of the indictment, and I have read it and studied it and understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can you confirm to me that the plea tendered on your behalf of not guilty to all charges by Mr. Scudder is the plea which you authorised him to tender?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I plead not guilty on all charges of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Please be seated again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, in light of the pleas tendered, the Registrar will be instructed to arrange in due course for a trial to take place on this indictment. Now, Mr. Hannis, can you assist me in relation to the implementation of your disclosure obligations. What stage have you reached?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We did disclose supporting material in this matter to the prior duty counsel, I believe that was Mr. Koppe, who appeared at Mr. Lukic's first appearance. We disclosed those materials on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I see that Rule 66(A)(ii) governs the disclosure or delivery of copies of the statements of the witnesses that the Prosecutor intends to call to testify at the trial and no doubt arrangements under that Rule are not normally made at this stage of the process, but this is a case which is well advanced in relation to other accused, on the view that the Prosecution seek to conjoin it with the proceedings against Milutinovic and others. Is there scope for an order or an arrangement to be made at this stage in relation to Rule 66(A)(ii)?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think there would be any problem with that. We've made disclosure to the other defendants in the related case in which we filed a motion to join this defendant. I see no reason that we couldn't provide those materials in fairly short order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when in ordinary course, in ordinary circumstances, where in the preparation period or the pre-trial period would these statements normally be delivered?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Normally, Your Honour, that would be done at the time we filed our pre-trial brief, our exhibit list, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From now, roughly how long is that normally? Just in very broad terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my limited experience, that range varies widely. It could be in a matter of a few months to many months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think what I'm inclined to do, Mr. Hannis, unless you try to persuade me otherwise, is in this case to make an order that within 30 days of today's appearance you should comply with Rule 66(A)(ii). Would that cause any particular difficulty?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I consult with my case manager? Your Honour, I'd like to try to persuade you to give us 60 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Scudder, is it likely that you will be the counsel in this case or is your tenure in the case necessarily for a limited period?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: My understanding is that we are in this case for the long-term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And have you received the supporting material from your predecessor?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have arrangements been put in hand to obtain it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: No. We can start work on that immediately after this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm fairly keen in this case to encourage -- I suppose you could describe it as catch-up, to make fairly rapid progress so that if there is to be union between this case and that of Milutinovic that the interests of the accused who have been before the Tribunal for some considerable time are not prejudiced by delays in relation to the present case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that regard I'm advised by my case manager we could provide a CD with the supporting materials to Mr. Scudder today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that assists me greatly. You've actually undermined your own position somewhat, Mr. Hannis, by making that offer, however. What I think I'll do in the circumstances is appoint the Prosecution to make available to the Defence the materials referred to in Rule 66(A)(ii) by the 30th of June. Now, that means, Mr. Scudder, that today you should have the supporting material, and within six to seven weeks you should have the statements and, therefore, be well-armed for your preparation purposes long before the first Status Conference, which will be about the beginning of September. Now, is there anything you, Mr. Scudder, wish to draw to my attention this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Not regarding any of the pre-trial matters, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: I think the Court should be aware of the special medical situation of the defendant. He underwent some -- two serious cardiac surgeries as recently as maybe four weeks ago, and I understand that his medical care may not be completely resolved. I think the Court should know about that because the surgery was very serious and it occurred in Serbia and delayed his removal to this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When I raised it -- or when the matter arose before, there was -- it was clear at that stage that adequate arrangements were being made. Are you suggesting otherwise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: In the brief conversations I've had with the defendant Lukic just in the last two days, he has indicated to me that he is being taken care of well through this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: But the local physicians need to consult from time to time with the cardiologist and the cardiac surgeon who performed the surgery on him in Serbia only a few weeks ago, and we were just concerned that that would continue. From my experience, he needs to have regular stress tests. One of those was interrupted. I believe he's had one since, but we are concerned that he will continue to have those as needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, one consequence of what I've been told this morning, that is that the supporting material was disclosed on the 20th of April, is that you have in the order of must just now be about 15 days to deal with preliminary motions, that deadline running from the date of disclosure. And I draw that to your attention because there is increasing anxiety among Judges in the Tribunal that the time scales set within the Rules should be adhered to, and this case is a fairly old case in spite of the fact that your client has been here only a short period of time, but experience in the case is well developed and therefore there is a pool of knowledge into which you can plug to enable you, I think, to ensure that preliminary motions are dealt with, at least made, within that time scale. Now, Mr. Lukic, could you stand again, please. Mr. Scudder has indicated a degree of concern about your medical condition. Is there anything that you wish to say about that to me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your microphone is -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have consulted my Defence counsel with respect to my health situation, and as during the last initial appearance, I said something about that and said that there was the possibility of including a physician specialist. That has taken place. It took place in April. A cardiologist came to see me, the cardiologist that provides medical services to the Tribunal, and in the meantime, on the basis of a prior agreement, I had physicians from Belgrade coming here. The cardiologist and surgeon who operated on me, they came to see me here. Now, since in mid-April or, rather, on the 13th or 14th -- or 12th, 13th, and 14th, to be exact, I have to say this, there was uncontrolled bleeding, and that is the difficult point in all this. They changed my therapy on the 15th, and I am now being administered this new therapy. The basic parameter of the blood or the blood levels have still not been brought to the necessary normal therapy level. Every Thursday they give me a blood test. I give my blood for analysis and I am expecting the results tomorrow, it being Thursday, because the doctors have told me that I need to be given this therapy for some time for the situation to improve. So I expect that the therapy will have done its work, but I'll leave that up to the physicians to determine. Thank you. Quite simply, it's a process that is ongoing for a certain period of time, especially when you are receiving new therapy. So we expect this new therapy to give off results. A month has gone by since the first tests were conducted, and the doctors feel that they have now got the situation in hand and that there is less likelihood of bleeding in the heart or the head, and of course the results of that kind of bleeding could be tragic. But I have full confidence in my physicians. I think that they are monitoring the situation, that they have my health situation under control, and I hope that my health situation will improve and be brought into acceptable levels if I adhere to the therapy given me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Clearly your care is in good hands, and you are particularly aware of the condition and are obviously aware of the need to draw to the physicians' attention any matter in relation to your health which is causing concern. The Rules of the Tribunal require that you should appear before me again in not more than 120 days from today. That's roughly at the beginning of September. So the case will come before me then when I will review progress in the case. Meanwhile, is there any other matter you wish to draw to my attention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in conjunction with the matter of preliminary motions, as you're aware, we had filed a motion to join this case with the Milutinovic, Ojdanic, Sainovic case. I believe we filed that motion about the time this accused arrived in court. So I'm not sure how you want to handle it in terms of Mr. Scudder being allowed to file some kind of response to that motion even though we filed it, I think, on the 5th of April, but I'm sure we would be happy to have input from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No doubt with -- no doubt, Mr. Hannis, with the CD of supporting material a copy of the joinder motion can be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. That's what I was just discussing with my case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scudder, you -- and indeed it would be helpful if you could also indicate the responses of the other accused such as they are so far. That could be sent as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think you'll find, Mr. Scudder, that the -- certainly the attitude of the accused whose responses I have seen is to accept that joinder as the appropriate course, but it would be helpful, I think, to the Trial Chamber if you were able at an early date to indicate your client's attitude to that motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Yes, we'd be happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scudder. Well, that appears -- anything else, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry, my case manager has brought to my attention that we do have a Status Conference regarding this defendant scheduled next week, on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the one on the 13th is for the accused Lazarevic. Does it follow that it should involve every accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: She's showing me a pleading with Lukic's name on the title page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My impression, Mr. Hannis, is that with the passage of time the two cases should be brought together. In fact, the three now; Lazarevic, Lukic, and Pavkovic. But for the purposes of next week, I suspect the appropriate course is to have a Status Conference only in relation to Lazarevic. However, in view of the doubt that's been cast just now, a Scheduling Order will be issued making the position clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The document does show both Lazarevic and Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I will consider the position once I rise, and issue a Scheduling Order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it does appear there is just the possibility you will be required next week because a Status Conference, the next stage in the process in court, has been arranged in the case of Lazarevic. But I doubt if that will be the case. However, an order will be made later today clarifying the position. I think that deals with that. That means that everything is dealt with and we can now adjourn.
